already_resolved.evidence: deploy/create_role.py rewritten to deprecation stub (commit 2456bb9, 2026-05-12). IAM role management moved to CDK stacks in infra/agentcore_runtime_role_stack.py. No raw stack traces possible.
model_adapters.py:290-325 now uses _ADAPTER_MAP dict ({"gemini": GeminiAdapter, "litellm": LiteLLMAdapter}) with registry-backed BedrockAdapter fallback. No hardcoded if/elif chains.
model_adapters.py:301-303 — empty string '' provider now produces clear error: 'Unknown MODEL_PROVIDER: ''' with supported list. No longer misleading.

bundles.name: negative-age-input-guard
bundles.intent: Add a date-ordering guard to deploy/app.py:_format_age_response() to prevent negative age output when parsing future dates of birth. Guard at line 172 before (today - dob).days computation, returning or raising a clear error message. Also add the same guard to agent.py's equivalent path for dual-file parity.

bundles.name: model-adapter-type-validation
bundles.intent: Constrain ModelCapabilities.runtimes from tuple[str, ...] to a typed Literal using the known allowed values ('local', 'deployed', 'planned'). Add a Pydantic-validated field or at minimum a runtime validation that catches invalid values at registry construction time instead of silently accepting any string.

bundles.name: model-adapter-registry-filters
bundles.intent: Harden the model_adapters.py registry: (1) planned_model_families() should filter on runtimes=('planned',) in addition to enabled=False so the intent is semantically accurate. (2) Normalize case in provider lookup with .lower() so 'Bedrock' and 'bedrock' resolve identically. (3) Add __all__ to control public symbols. (4) Add a unit test that verifies the duplicate-key guard at line 166-167 actually fires on a malformed registry.

bundles.name: model-adapter-validation-fixes
bundles.intent: Address three low-risk validation gaps in model_adapters.py: (1) Move supported_local_providers() out of ValueError f-strings to avoid double-fault risk on registry failure. (2) Broaden MOONSHOT_API_KEY validation beyond prefix-only check (verify expected key format). (3) Validate LITELLM_API_BASE path component (e.g. require /v1 suffix) so misconfigured URLs produce clear errors at init time rather than at runtime.

bundles.name: test-hygiene-cleanup
bundles.intent: Clean up five test-quality issues in test_model_adapters.py and test_app.py: (1) Refactor copy-pasted planned-family rejection tests into @pytest.mark.parametrize. (2) Convert class-level mutable _env dict to fixture with factory. (3) Remove test_litellm_rejection_occurs_before_bedrock_call (subset of existing test). (4-5) Two deferred items from the 4-5 review batch: fix test fragility.

bundles.name: documentation-clarity-fixes
bundles.intent: Fix documentation gaps and brittle test assertions: (1) Update the stale 3-1-comprehensive-readme.md artifact to match current ARM64 packaging convention. (2) Add concrete Bedrock model ID to deploy/verify.py Llama failure hint. (3) Decouple TestReadmeProviderRoadmap assertions from Markdown syntax by matching on content not formatting. (4-6) Remaining doc/structure nits from 4-5 review.

skip.reason: self._client_args or None pattern is intentionally tested (test line 542 asserts this behavior). {} → None conversion is by design, not a defect.
"local" not in cap.runtimes guard at model_adapters.py:313-317 is a deliberate defensive guard protecting against future registry misconfiguration. Not dead code in the architectural sense.
Gemini branch reached only after registry checks is by design — the registry validates existence and enablement first, then routes to the adapter map. Architectural intentional, not a bug.
bedrock_first=False provider without adapter falls to safety ValueError. By-design guard, would only fire on registry misconfiguration.
README matrix split is a presentation choice with all information present. Reviewer noted 'all information is present; restructuring would be significant churn.' Not a defect to fix automatically.

decisions.question: Should the README model-support roadmap and verification tables be merged into a single consolidated matrix, or keep the current two-table structure?
decisions.context: README.md lines 460-487: The roadmap table (stage/providers/status) and verification table (provider/level/notes) cover different dimensions with explanatory prose between them. Consolidating would reduce context switching but the original reviewer noted 'all information present; restructuring would be significant churn.'

options.label: Merge into single matrix
options.intent: Consolidate the roadmap and verification tables into one unified provider matrix with columns: Provider, Stage, Local Support, Deployed Support, Verification Level, Notes.

options.label: Keep current structure, rename sections
options.intent: Keep two tables but rename section headers for clarity and add cross-references so readers understand the relationship.

options.label: Keep as-is
options.resolution: All information is present and accurate. Restructuring is cosmetic.

decisions.question: Should the test_litellm_rejection_occurs_before_bedrock_call test at test_app.py:408 be removed as a duplicate, or kept for documentation purposes?
decisions.context: This test only asserts mock_client.assert_not_called() which is already asserted by test_litellm_provider_rejected_by_deployed_runtime at line 400. It adds zero unique coverage but documents the intent that pre-runtime rejection avoids Bedrock API calls.

options.label: Keep as documentation artifact
options.resolution: No functional issue; the test is harmless and documents intent.
